In Śākambharī. VisnuSm 85-21; śākaṃbharyām //
At Phalgutīrtha, Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.22.
In the Mahāgaṅgā. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.23)
In a village consisting of three ploughs.
At Kumāradhārā.
At Prabhāsa.
Wherever [one may be] on the Sarasvatī, especially so.
At Gaṅgādvāra. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.28)
And at Prayāga.
At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.
Always in the Naimiṣa forest.
Especially at Vārāṇasī.
In the hermitage of Agastya.
In the hermitage of Kaṇva. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.34)
In the Kauśikī river. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.35)
On the bank of the Sarayū.
At the confluence of the Soṇa and the Jyotiṣā.
At Śrīparvata, Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.38.
In Kālodaka.
At Uttaramānasa.
In the case of a mare, [the rule is] as follows.
In the Matanga-vāpī [well].
[The gift] for the Seven Sages. VisnuSm 85-43.
In the footprint of Viṣṇu.
[It is] on the steps of the path to heaven. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.45)
At the Godāvarī. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.46)
In the Gomatī river. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.47)
In the Vetravatī river.
In the Vipāśā river.
In the Vitastā river. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.50)
On the bank of the Śatadrū river.
[One obtains this] on the Candrabhāgā river.
In the Irāvatī river. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.53)
On the bank of the Sindhu river.
In the south, at Pañcanada.
He should cause [the victim] to be sacrificed.
In these and other such sacred fords (tīrthas), as well as others...
In the best of rivers.
In all their respective natures as well.
On sandbanks. (Viṣṇusmṛti 85.60)
In mountain springs. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.61)
On mountains. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.62)
In the groves. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.63)
In the forests. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.64)
In groves. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 85.65)
In houses smeared with cow dung.
In pleasant places. (Viṣṇusmṛti 85.67)
And in this regard, there are these verses sung by the ancestors:
"May that being be born in our family who shall offer us handfuls of water,
especially in rivers containing abundant cool water."
"May there arise in our lineage some preeminent man who,
with a concentrated mind, shall perform for us the śrāddha at the Vaṭa tree on Gayāśīrṣa."
Many sons should be desired, so that even if only one among them goes to Gayā,
or performs the Aśvamedha sacrifice, or sets free a dark-colored bull.
Viṣṇu Smṛti 86:
Now follows the ritual of the release of a bull (vṛṣotsarga).
On the full moon day of Kārttika or Āśvayuja.
In that regard, at the very outset, one should examine the bull.
The son of a cow that has a living calf and is full of milk.
Endowed with all auspicious characteristics.
Blue. VisnuSm 86-06.
Or one that is red, with the face, tail, feet, and horns white.
One who conceals a herd [of cattle].

Then, having strewn grass around a well-kindled fire in the midst of cows, and having cooked a *caru* offering for Pūṣan with milk, and having offered oblations with the mantra, "May Pūṣan follow our cows; may there be delight here," the blacksmith shall brand the bull.
On one side with a discus, and on the other side with a trident.
One should bathe the marked [image] with the four verses beginning with "hiraṇyavarṇāḥ" and with the verse "saṃ no devīḥ."
Having brought him who has bathed and is adorned, together with four heifers that have also bathed and are adorned, one should recite the Rudra hymns, the Puruṣasūkta, and the Kūṣmāṇḍī verses.
One should recite "The father of the calves" into the right ear of the bull.
And this [verse] as well. (Viṣṇu Smṛti 86.14)
For the Blessed Lord Dharma is proclaimed as the Bull with four feet;
I choose him with devotion—may he protect me in every way.

"I give this young man to you as your husband; sport and move about with him, your beloved. O King Soma, may we not be deprived of our offspring nor of our bodies, and may we not fall into the power of the enemy."
One should have a bull accompanied by a heifer placed in the northeast direction;
one should give the officiating priest (hotṛ) a pair of garments, as well as gold and a vessel of white copper.
To the iron-worker, a wage should be given according to his heart's desire;
he should provide food with plenty of clarified butter and feed Brāhmaṇas there as well.
In whatever reservoir of water a bull that has been set free drinks,
that entire reservoir of water stands as an offering for his ancestors.
Wherever a proud bull scratches the earth with its horn,
there abundant food and drink for the ancestors is presented.

Now, on the full moon day of Vaiśākha, having prepared a black antelope skin with its hooves and horns— its horns adorned with gold, its hooves with silver, and its tail decorated with pearls— one should spread it upon a woolen cloth.
Then, one should cover it with sesame seeds.
And one should make it with a golden navel.
One should cover [the body] with a pair of unwashed garments.
And one should have it adorned with all kinds of perfumes and jewels.

Having visualized four metallic vessels filled with milk, curd, honey, and clarified butter in the four directions, he should give them to a Brāhmaṇa who maintains the sacred fires, who is adorned and covered with a pair of garments.
And on this point, there are these verses:
But he who gives a black antelope skin together with its hooves and horns,
having covered it with sesame seeds and cloths, and adorned it with all kinds of jewels;
By him, the earth—along with its oceans, caves, mountains, forests, and groves, extending to the four quarters—is considered as given; of this there is no doubt.
He who places sesame seeds upon a black antelope skin, along with gold, honey, and clarified butter,
and gives them to a Brahmin, overcomes all evil deeds.
Now, a cow that is giving birth becomes the earth.
Having given her, adorned with ornaments, to a Brāhmaṇa, one obtains the fruit of the gift of the earth.
On this point, there is a verse:
Having given a cow with her calf and facing both ways, one who is faithful and composed attains heaven for as many yugas as there are hairs on their bodies.
The month of Kārttika has Agni as its presiding deity.
And fire is the mouth of all the gods.

Therefore, by bathing outdoors during the month of Kārttika, being devoted to the recitation of the Gāyatrī, and eating sacrificial food (haviṣya) only once [a day], one becomes purified from the sins committed throughout the year.
One who bathes daily throughout the entire month of Kārttika, having conquered his senses,
reciting [sacred mantras], eating sacrificial food (haviṣya), and being self-controlled, is liberated from all sins.

On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, when it is conjoined with the asterism Mṛgaśiras, one should cause a Brāhmaṇa to receive at moonrise one *prastha* of powdered salt with a golden center.
By this rite, one is born endowed with beauty and good fortune.

If the full moon day of Pauṣa should coincide with the Puṣya asterism, on that day one whose body has been rubbed with a paste of white mustard seeds, who has been consecrated with a jar filled with cow's ghee, and who has bathed with all medicinal herbs, all fragrances, and all seeds— having bathed the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva with ghee, having worshipped him with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth, and having offered oblations into the fire with Vaiṣṇava, Śākra, and Bārhaspatya mantras— should cause the Brāhmaṇas to pronounce blessings with ghee mixed with gold.
One should give a pair of garments to the performer.
By this rite, one is nourished.
If the full moon day of Māgha is joined with the Maghā nakṣatra, by performing a śrāddha with sesame seeds on that day, one becomes purified.

If the full moon day of Phālguna is joined with the asterism Phalgunī, by offering on that day to a Brāhmaṇa a well-prepared and well-spread bed, one obtains a wife who is pleasing to the mind, beautiful, and wealthy.
A woman [should also behave thus] toward her husband.
If the full moon day of Caitra is joined with the asterism Citrā, one attains good fortune by giving beautiful garments on that day.

If the Vaiśākhī full moon is conjoined with the Viśākhā nakṣatra, by satiating seven Brahmins on that day with sesame seeds mixed with honey and thereby pleasing Dharmarāja, one becomes purified from sins.
If the full moon day of Jyeṣṭha should coincide with the Jyeṣṭhā nakṣatra, by the gift of an umbrella and sandals on that day, one attains lordship over cattle.
On the full moon day of Āṣāḍha that is conjoined with the Āṣāḍhā nakṣatra, by the gift of food and drink, one obtains that very same merit in an inexhaustible manner.
On the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa joined with the asterism Śravaṇā, by giving a water-cow together with food, covered with a pair of garments, one attains heaven.
On the full moon day of Prauṣṭhapada, when it is conjoined with the Proṣṭhapadā nakṣatra, one becomes liberated from all sins by the gift of a cow.
On the full moon day of Āśvayuja, when the moon is in the constellation Aśvinī, by giving a vessel filled with ghee and accompanied by gold to a Brahmin, one becomes possessed of a radiant fire.

If the full moon day of Kārttika should coincide with the Kṛttikā constellation, one should, at the rising of the moon marked by the six signs, give to a Brāhmaṇa a white bull or one of another color, endowed with all kinds of grain, jewels, and perfumes, in the midst of lamps; having done so, one shall not behold the fear of the wilderness.

On the third day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, having fasted, worshipped Śrī Vāsudeva with unbroken grains (akṣatas), and offered those same grains as oblations and given them away, one becomes purified from all sins.
And whatever one gives on that day, that attains imperishability.

When the full moon of Pauṣa has passed, on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight, one who has fasted, bathed with sesame seeds, offered a libation of water with sesame seeds, worshipped Vāsudeva with sesame seeds, offered oblations of those same sesame seeds, and given them away and eaten them, becomes purified from sins.

When the full moon of Māgha has passed, on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight, one who has observed a fast, having reached the Śravaṇa asterism, should offer two lamps with two great wicks before Śrī Vāsudeva.
On the right side, having offered a complete garment dyed with saffron and a balance of ghee increased by eight [units], he should proceed.
On the left side, having placed a vessel containing sesame oil along with eight [other items], covered entirely with a white cloth; ViṣṇuSm 90.22.
Having performed this, in whatever kingdom, in whatever region, or in whatever family one is born, one becomes radiant therein.
Having given ghee daily to Brahmins throughout the entire month of Āśvina and having gratified the two Aśvins, one becomes a possessor of beauty.
In that very month, by feeding Brāhmaṇas daily with products of the cow, one becomes a sharer in a kingdom.

Every month, when the moon is in conjunction with the asterism Revatī, one who feeds Brahmins with the supreme food—payasa mixed with honey and ghee—for the sake of pleasing Revatī, and thereby gratifies Revatī, becomes a possessor of beauty.
Having offered oblations of sesame seeds into the fire every day during the month of Māgha, and having fed Brahmins with kulmāṣa mixed with ghee, one becomes possessed of a radiant digestive fire.
Having bathed in river water on every fourteenth day (Caturdaśī) and having worshipped Dharmarāja, one becomes purified from all sins.
If one desires abundant enjoyments that endure as long as the moon and sun,
one should always bathe in the morning during the two months of Māgha and Phālguna.
VisnuSm 91:
Now, for one who has constructed a well, half of his evil deeds is destroyed when water begins to flow from it.
The maker of a tank, being eternally satisfied, enjoys the world of Varuṇa.
The giver of water is always satisfied.
For one who plants trees, those trees become his sons in the next world.
One who gives trees gratifies the gods with the flowers of those trees.
And one should honor guests with fruits.
And one should honor those who have arrived with one's shadow.
When it rains from the sky, one satisfies the ancestors with water.
One who constructs a bridge attains heaven.
One who builds a temple for a deity attains the very world of that deity for whom he constructs the temple.
Having plastered it with lime, he shines with glory.
Having performed a variegated [sacrifice], one attains the world of the Gandharvas.
By the offering of flowers, one becomes possessed of splendor.
By the gift of unguents, one becomes possessed of fame.
By the offering of a lamp, one becomes possessed of keen vision and radiant everywhere.
By the gift of food, one becomes strong.
By removing the remains of offerings made to the gods, one obtains the fruit of gifting a cow.
[One attains merit] from sweeping the temple of a deity, from smearing it [with cow dung], from cleaning the remnants of a Brāhmaṇa's meal, from washing the feet, and from attending to the sick.
One who performs the rite of restoration for wells, groves, tanks,
and temples obtains the original merit.
The granting of fearlessness is superior to all forms of giving.
By giving that, one attains the desired world.
And by the gift of land.
By giving even a piece of land the size of a cow-hide, one becomes purified from all sins.
By the gift of a cow, one attains the heavenly world.
One who gives ten cows attains the worlds of the cows.
The giver of a hundred cows [attains] the worlds of Brahmā.

Having given a cow with golden horns, silver hooves, a pearl-adorned tail, a bronze milking vessel, and a cloth as an upper garment, one attains the heavenly world for as many years as there are hairs on that cow.
Especially [the gift of] a Kapila cow.
Having given a tamed bull capable of bearing the yoke, one becomes the donor of ten cows.
The giver of a horse attains the same world as the Sun.
The giver of clothing attains the same world as Candra (the Moon).
By the gift of gold, one attains residence in the same world as Agni.
